audit_findings.title: Potential double counting of equity-method investees
audit_findings.magnitude: $364 million of 2025 equity-method earnings and $2.146 billion stakes bridge; if the full $364 million is embedded in the anchor, computed operating-PV overlap is approximately $4.33 billion bear, $5.11 billion base and $6.04 billion bull
audit_findings.mechanism: Net income contributes equity-method earnings to OE while stakes_net separately adds the underlying investments to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our share of the results from joint ventures, affiliated companies and alliances is reported in our Consolidated Statements of Net Income as equity, royalty and interest income from investees, and is reported net of all applicable income taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that equity-method earnings enter net income and that 2025 Cummins-share earnings were $364 million, separate from $105 million of royalty and interest income. The valuation says portfolio interest income was purged but does not show that equity-method earnings were purged before adding $2.146 billion of stakes. Actual double counting therefore remains unproven without the OE worksheet, but the potential overlap equals 21.4% of the $1.701 billion anchor and is reasonably capable of changing intrinsic value materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 OE worksheet line by line; separately remove the $364 million equity-method earnings while retaining only qualifying operating royalties, then rerun all scenarios with stakes_net added once.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded Amplify contribution omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $418 million, equal to $3.00 per share and 1.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A future equity-investee funding obligation should reduce stakes_net or future OE if it is not already forecast as an investment outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we contributed $412 million and our maximum remaining required contribution to the joint venture was $418 million, which could be reduced by future government incentives received by the joint venture.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q confirms that the full $418 million contractual commitment remained outstanding at June 30, 2026, with uncertain timing. No bridge offset is shown, so the omission is demonstrated unless it was included in forecast OE. Even deducting the unreduced maximum would lower base value only from $215.15 to about $212.15 per share and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $556.275 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether any of the $418 million is included in forecast OE or stakes_net and document expected incentives; if absent, deduct the present value in the bridge even though the maximum adjustment is not conclusion-changing.

audit_findings.title: Contingent buyout obligations for partially owned distributors
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecognized or unnetted distributor put obligations are claims on common equity and would reduce the stakes bridge or other equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: In certain cases where we own a partial interest in a distributor, we may be obligated to purchase the other equity holders' interests if certain events occur (such as the death or resignation of the distributor principal or a change in control of Cummins Inc.).
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that repurchase obligations exist but supplies neither current settlement values nor triggering probabilities. The record therefore cannot determine whether the aggregate claim is material. This is an unresolved contingent exposure, not a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Inventory each distributor put or repurchase clause, identify triggering events, estimate fair-value settlement amounts and probabilities, and reconcile them to recognized liabilities and stakes_net before rerunning the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Parent-income numerator may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income combined with consolidated D&A, capital expenditure and working-capital adjustments can assign minority-owned cash economics to Cummins shareholders, affecting historical OE, the anchor and growth framing.
audit_findings.evidence: The noncontrolling ownership interest in our income, net of tax, is classified as net income attributable to noncontrolling interests in our Consolidated Statements of Net Income .
audit_findings.explanation: The basis mismatch is plausible because the filing reports consolidated cash flows but separately deducts NCI income of $114 million in 2025, $122 million in 2024 and $105 million in 2023. Those income amounts do not quantify the NCI share of D&A, capex or working-capital movements, and the supplied record does not provide a consistent parent-basis OE reconstruction. The direction can vary by year, although an excess consolidated add-back would overstate OE.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year on a consolidated basis followed by explicit deductions for the NCI shares of earnings, D&A, capex and working-capital movements, then recompute the anchor, trend and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may not be fully distributable without tax friction
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.808 billion of international cash and marketable securities at 2026-06-30; actual haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding taxes, transfer restrictions and minimum operating-cash requirements reduce the $3.924 billion cash/STI bridge addition available to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: If we distribute our foreign cash balances to the U.S. or to other foreign subsidiaries, we could be required to accrue and pay withholding taxes, for example, if we repatriated cash from certain foreign subsidiaries whose earnings we asserted are completely or partially permanently reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing identifies $2.808 billion, or 71.6%, of cash and marketable securities as international and confirms possible withholding taxes on certain permanently reinvested foreign earnings. It does not provide the jurisdictional tax basis, restrictions or required operating cash, so the actual haircut and its materiality cannot be established. The exposed pool is large enough that the issue cannot be dismissed.
audit_findings.action: Map the $3.924 billion balance by legal entity and jurisdiction, calculate filed-law withholding and other leakage, identify restricted and minimum operating cash, and rerun the bridge using only net distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor and null perimeter may not represent the post-Accelera business
audit_findings.magnitude: $458 million of 2025 Accelera charges, including $415 million noncash and $43 million cash; $199 million additional 2026 charge associated with a $175 million net payment
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring charges can depress anchor OE, while continuing Accelera losses, fulfillment costs, commitments and disposal payments can reduce post-exit OE; a null perimeter fails to align these effects.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of market conditions and the current business outlook, we intend to stop new commercial activity in the electrolyzer space, subject to information and consultation in accordance with local legal requirements.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 charges equal 26.9% of the $1.701 billion anchor, so their classification can materially affect operating value. The subsequent 10-Q demonstrates a changed perimeter: Cummins sold the low-pressure fuel-cell business, paid $175 million net and recorded a $199 million charge. Accelera also reported a $346 million first-half 2026 EBITDA loss, including that charge, and a $69 million second-quarter loss, demonstrating that losses did not end with the 2025 impairments. The net valuation direction cannot be determined until one-offs and continuing cash economics are separated.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 OE by adding back only genuinely nonrecurring noncash charges, retain cash restructuring and fulfillment costs, incorporate the 2026 disposal payment and continuing post-exit losses, define the post-Accelera perimeter explicitly, and rerun all scenarios.
